assignedChecks.after: Bing and I differ in rank and are far apart in our positions; moreover, he and his brothers are close relatives of the imperial house. By rights I ought to defer and accommodate myself to the circumstances.

Reading the histories, I see maternal relatives indulged and allowed to wield power and disorder the court: first they enjoy extraordinary glory, then suffer the consequences of holding positions beyond their station. This is what is meant by love proving sufficient to cause harm.

I have often resented that successive rulers did not fully master the means of preventing incipient trouble while preserving favor to the end. Why not establish these relatives with a territorial fief and let their descendants inherit the vassal state, as with Qi and Chen under Zhou?

Though deficient in virtue, I undeservedly received appointment as one of the former emperor’s generals. With the people of only several commanderies, I still aspire to engulf powerful enemies. Thus, from recent times until now we have crossed weapons in battle, farming for one season and fighting for three; yet our troops are not exhausted, our granaries have surplus grain, our enemies fear us more each day, and our territory grows daily. How much greater, then, are imperial majesty and its imposing power—how could the two be compared!

Though deficient in virtue, I undeservedly received the former emperor's appointment among the generals; with the people of several commanderies I still wish to swallow powerful enemies; therefore from recent times until now, crossing weapons and meeting blades, one season for farming and three for war, yet the troops are not exhausted, the granaries have surplus grain, the enemy fears us more each day and our territory grows daily; how much greater, then, are imperial majesty and its imposing power—how could the two be compared!

Remembering past events provides a guide for the future. Yet Yu Bing, Director of the Secretariat and General of the Left, and his fellows control the central levers of government within and hold senior military commands outside; the brothers stand side by side in office, with no other ministers to match them.

Past events, if not forgotten, are a model for later affairs; yet Yu Bing, Director of the Secretariat and General of the Left, and his fellows grasp the pivot within and hold senior military commands outside; the brothers stand side by side, with no other minister to match them.

Your Majesty deeply honors family ties; Bing and his fellows ought naturally to look up in expectation.
Your Majesty deeply honors the ties of Weiyang; Bing and the others ought themselves to stretch their necks in expectation.

I have often said: if a ruler wishes to honor maternal kin, enfeoff them in vassal states, enrich their stipends, and limit their power so that the throne shows no partial favor and the realm no private suspicion.

Your servant often says: if a ruler of the age wishes to honor the maternal clan, why not enfeoff them with vassal states, enrich their stipends and gifts, and limit their power and advantage, so that above there is no partial favor and below no private talk.

Your servant and Bing and the others differ in rank and status and are far apart in our situations; moreover, they are close kin of the imperial house. By rights I ought to defer and accommodate myself to the circumstances.

Again he wrote to Bing, saying: You, by the intimacy of the empress's chamber and closeness as maternal kin, hold the pivot in total, issue and receive royal commands, and together hold the posts of generals and provincial overseers; your brothers spread a net, displayed across the capital region.

Whenever I read the histories, I see maternal relatives invariably pampered and indulged, allowed to hold power and disorder the court; first they enjoy glory surpassing their age, then incur the burden of riding when unfit; this is what is meant by love being sufficient to cause harm.

I often resent that rulers of successive ages did not fully use the art of preventing incipient trouble and preserving favor to the end; why not establish them with a territorial fief and let the vassal states be inherited in succession, as with Qi and Chen under Zhou?
Worthy men rallied to them; although eunuchs brought them into peril, the realm lamented them because they could nonetheless conduct themselves without arrogance and gave their lives for the state.

Worthy men gave them their hearts; although they were endangered by eunuch minions, the realm lamented them, because they were still able to conduct themselves without arrogance and took thought for the state at the cost of their lives.

Bing, seeing the memorial and letter, was greatly afraid; because Huang was extremely far away and beyond his power to control, he thereupon, with He Chong and the others, memorialized to permit Huang to style himself King of Yan.
After Fen died, the emperor gnashed his teeth in later regret.

Emperor Cheng was dim and weak, unable to stand on his own; inwardly confused by a beautiful wife, outwardly indulging the five maternal uncles, he finally let Wang Mang take the imperial throne without effort.

Formerly Xu Fu set forth the warning of the Huo clan; Emperor Xuan did not follow it, so that even loyal ministers became a rebellious lineage, truly because investigation was not careful and precautions were not taken at the first signs.
